retrieved_cards.title: Disassembly can desync and show a plausible-but-wrong instruction stream
retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: Instructions are being read at a fixed alignment where the real code overlaps, jumps into the middle of an instruction, or uses anti-disassembly, so the decoded stream may not be what executes.
retrieved_cards.mechanism: A byte stream has multiple decodings; a linear or fixed-offset decode can lock onto the wrong one, producing instructions that look real but are not executed as shown.
retrieved_cards.validation_note: Follow control flow into the region to fix the instruction boundaries, and re-disassemble at that alignment; where two decodings are possible, the one an incoming edge lands on is the one that runs.

retrieved_cards.applicability_signal: A byte-wise XOR with a constant (single-byte, repeating, or position-dependent key) is applied to the input before it is compared against a constant byte sequence.

retrieved_cards.validation_note: Read the key and whether it is single-byte, repeating, or position-dependent; XOR the target back; then XOR the recovered input forward again and check it reproduces the compared bytes exactly.

minimum_evidence_before_use: an XOR operation is observed between the input and the comparison
the XOR operand (key) is identifiable or recoverable
